answer: Provers first lock 64 GB of volatile memory to an on-chain anchor seed. Verifiers challenge nodes to execute sequential cache-line traversals across pseudo-random RAM offsets within strict 80-nanosecond windows. Agents fold traversed lines into a mirror buffer, cryptographically sealing the path before outputting through an egress jetty. Stalled access or corrupt seals trigger immediate bond slashing and eviction. Simulating one hundred agents requires 6.4 terabytes of dedicated DDR5 memory, imposing an unforgeable $19,000 hardware barrier.
